response: {"headline": "SPIRE-2 was stopped early by Pfizer in November 2016 due to anti-drug antibodies attenuating bococizumab's LDL-C lowering, making development non-viable — an execution failure despite an observed HR of 0.79 (21% RRR) that exceeded the calculator's predicted HR of 0.838.", "summary": "The SPIRE-2 trial randomized 10,621 high-risk patients to bococizumab or placebo and was stopped early at a median 12-month follow-up after 403 primary endpoint events (179 treatment, 224 control). The observed hazard ratio of 0.79 (21% relative risk reduction) was better than the calculator's expected HR of 0.838 (16.2% RRR) based on a phase 2 placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of -53.4 mg/dL and 42.5% power. However, Pfizer discontinued development on November 1, 2016 because anti-drug antibodies caused attenuation of LDL-C lowering over time — a drug-specific immunogenicity issue, not a failure of the PCSK9 mechanism. No confidence interval was reported for the primary HR, and the composite endpoint included a softer component (hospitalization for unstable angina requiring urgent revascularization).
